correctness.rationale: The kernel is integrated independently by block formulas and a causal convolution recurrence. At fixed middle length the derivative is 4(1-e^{-b})(e^{-c}-e^{-a}), forcing unique symmetry. Along the symmetric subfamily the derivative has the sign of 2b+2log cosh(b/2)-L, an everywhere strictly increasing function with a unique root in (0,L). This establishes the complete global minimum including boundaries. Strict fractional bounds, monotonic shift, asymptotics and CPMG gap follow algebraically. The standalone checker passed 3,509 independent numerical comparisons; computations verify finite cases, not replace the proof.

value.rationale: Two-pulse Carr–Purcell/Uhrig placement is a central baseline for coherence protection. The theorem identifies the globally optimal continuous timing for a natural finite-memory Gaussian bath and proves that the standard zero-area pair is always strictly inferior, with a monotone crossover from quarter to one-third first-pulse fraction. The theorem provides an exact, reproducible rule and a sharp physical boundary between static-noise cancellation and finite-correlation optimality. This is a meaningful idealized control-design classification, not a parameter restatement or a finite-grid lookup.
